title: CMSTP spawns a child process
description: Detects a child process created by CMSTP. Legitimate profile installers can invoke helper programs, so the child and INF content require review before escalation.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may use CMSTP to proxy execution through a signed Windows binary.
hypothesis.rationale: CMSTP can proxy attacker-controlled INF commands, but legitimate profile packages can also create helper processes. Parent-child telemetry is useful for hunting and triage, not a standalone high-confidence verdict.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify any process whose direct initiating process is cmstp.exe while leaving CMSTP launch events, unrelated parent processes and incomplete events unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Inspect the spawned program and Connection Manager INF before escalation; approved installer helper execution can produce this same relationship.
steps: Baseline this signal with the responsible application or endpoint owner; legitimate use is expected, and this event alone is not a compromise verdict.
Review the child image, command line, signer, account, device role and the complete CMSTP parent command.
Inspect the referenced INF or profile package and correlate file creation, network retrieval, persistence and follow-on processes.
Confirm an approved Connection Manager deployment; otherwise isolate the endpoint and investigate the originating file and user activity.
false_positives: Rare approved Connection Manager profile packages that intentionally invoke a helper process

validation.expected_outcome: Match processes directly spawned by cmstp.exe; do not match CMSTP itself, another parent or events without the parent field.

limitations: This single-event signal does not establish malicious intent or successful execution. Renamed binaries, alternate tools, obfuscation and unlogged activity can evade the bounded predicates.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
